CCRF Research Workspace

Use the official Lipedema Foundation Common Case Report Form Version 1 data dictionaries to structure consistent research records. LipoScope preserves the source variable names, question wording, coded choices, validation settings, required-field definitions and branching expressions used by the embedded CCRF schema. Direct identifiers are not stored, and LipoScope does not diagnose a patient or replace an institutionally governed data-capture system.

CCRF Research Workspace

Build consistent research records using the official Lipedema Foundation CCRF Version 1, check required fields and export coded or readable datasets. The workspace follows the embedded CCRF Version 1 source definitions and keeps entered research records in the current browser.

✓

About the CCRF workspace

The workspace uses the official CCRF classifications, field names, response options, validation rules and branching supplied by the Lipedema Foundation. Conditional questions are ordinary CCRF questions: they appear when their official condition is met and are not excluded for privacy reasons.

Official CCRF Version 1

Core, Supplemental Highly Recommended, Supplemental and Exploratory data dictionaries are included with their official variable names, field types, coded responses and required-field rules.

Open the official CCRF page · Read the CCRF development paper

Local records and research exports

Participant responses are stored in the current browser workspace. Users can review missing or invalid required fields and download coded, readable, long-format, dictionary and data-quality files.

CRF

Standardized Cohort Builder

Select an official CCRF classification and complete its source-defined participant and clinical fields. LipoScope shows required-field completion, missing or invalid responses, and saved-record summaries.

Research-use note: use a study identifier for browser-local records and enter identifiable information in the study's governed data-capture system. LipoScope does not diagnose a patient.
△

Cohort Design Gap Radar

Review the active CCRF record and saved records by official form and section. The Radar highlights required fields that need completion or correction and shows source-version differences.

How to use it: open any section with missing or invalid required fields, complete the highlighted questions in the Standardized Cohort Builder, and return to confirm the updated record and cohort status.
☷

CCRF Data Dictionary and Dataset Export

Understand how Standardized Cohort Builder responses are coded, compare the active record with the official CCRF dictionary, and download analysis-ready and human-readable research files.

How entered responses become research data

CCRF response codes provide consistent database values; readable labels explain what each code means. Both are generated from the same official field definition used by the Standardized Cohort Builder.

Recommended: complete research package

Downloads one ZIP containing coded data, readable data, paired codes and labels, long-format records, the official data dictionary, a data-quality report and a source manifest.

For statistical analysis

Use CCRF_records_coded.csv together with CCRF_data_dictionary.csv in R, Python, SPSS, Stata or another governed research environment.

For clinical or manual review

Use CCRF_records_codes_and_labels.csv or CCRF_records_human_readable.csv so every response can be interpreted without looking up numeric codes separately.

Files included in the complete research package
  • CCRF_records_codes_and_labels.csv - paired official codes and readable answers.
  • CCRF_records_coded.csv - analysis-ready official codes.
  • CCRF_records_human_readable.csv - readable answers.
  • CCRF_records_long.csv - one field per row with code, label, status and source metadata.
  • CCRF_data_dictionary.csv - variable definitions, codes, validation and branching.
  • CCRF_data_quality_report.csv - missing, invalid, privacy-excluded, inactive-branch and version-mismatched entries.
  • CCRF_source_manifest.txt - LipoScope version, CCRF version, classifications and source checksums.
Official CCRF classifications: Core, Supplemental Highly Recommended, Supplemental and Exploratory provide progressively more inclusive sets of data elements. The Lipedema Foundation recommends using the longest form feasible for the study design.

🔍 Auto-Discovery Engine Auto

Automatically search PubMed across all 10 research topics, while enforcing a strict lipedema/lipoedema disease scope. Topic terms such as lymphatic, adipose, hormone, or fibrosis are only accepted when the record also discusses lipedema/lipoedema. Results are classified from title + abstract text and deduplicated before import.

📊 Live Database Summary PubMed · canonical lipedema/lipoedema query

These counts use the same canonical PubMed disease query as Analytics: title or abstract occurrences of lipedema/lipoedema and NLM-listed entry terms, plus lipohyperplasia dolorosa and records indexed with the Lipedema MeSH heading. Record-level analytics use paginated retrieval rather than a fixed record cap. The “Curated Papers” count reflects your visible Browse workspace.

📖 About This Resource

LipoScope supports research into lipoedema (lipedema), a chronic painful adipose-tissue disorder where delayed recognition, inconsistent case definitions, small cohorts, limited objective measures, and fragmented genetics evidence still slow progress.

The public default Browse collection contains 200 lipoedema/lipedema papers spanning 2009–2026, combining a manually curated seed with a PubMed-expanded metadata layer. Each record includes topic and study-type classification, source links, open-access figure lookup where full-text access supports it, and optional local PDF-based figure preview in the browser. Study-type classification uses NLM Publication Type metadata, identity-verified PMC article type, MeSH study-design descriptors, structured abstract Methods/design evidence, and available PMC Methods evidence. The Browse filters include research designs and publication formats such as editorials, letters, protocols, meeting abstracts, corrections and technical articles. Records that cannot be resolved are labelled Unresolved category for topic or Unclassified / Other for study type. Uploaded PDFs remain in the user's local workspace.

The CCRF Workspace provides official CCRF Version 1 classifications for standardised data entry, required-field review, saved-record summaries, data-dictionary inspection and de-identified exports. The Analytics tab separates whole-field PubMed signals from the visible Browse workspace, and Live Search lets users add new PubMed records with one click.

📝 How to Cite and Reuse LipoScope

If you use LipoScope in research, teaching, presentations, or scholarly work, please cite the software repository and, when available, the associated publication, alongside the relevant primary papers surfaced through the app.

Preferred Software Citation
Cildir S. (2026). LipoScope (Version 1.0.0) [Software].
https://github.com/LipoScope/LipoScope_v1.0.0
GitHub citation metadata is provided in CITATION.cff. The organisation repository also contains the CCRF source-to-schema workflow, browser tests and deterministic release-build instructions. When the journal article becomes available, please cite both the software and the publication.

LipoScope software code is released under the MIT License. Original LipoScope documentation and generated evidence summaries are available under CC BY 4.0. Official CCRF material, publications, PubMed records, abstracts, external links, paper figures and other third-party content retain their original ownership and terms and are not relicensed by LipoScope.

🏷️ Research Topic Categories exact PubMed category-query counts · categories may overlap

Topic links and displayed category counts use the same exact high-precision PubMed queries. Record-level categorisation combines disease-specific and Major Topic MeSH evidence, exact category-query PMID membership, precise titles, author keywords, indexed substances, structured abstract sections, and identity-verified PMC evidence where available. LipoScope retains secondary topic matches internally and assigns one primary topic only when the leading evidence is sufficiently strong and distinct; records awaiting indexing, lacking usable metadata, or carrying equivalent multi-domain evidence remain in the Unresolved category with the reason counted separately.

👤 Public Mode & Optional Local Profile

LipoScope opens immediately in Public Local Mode. No registration, login, account, server, or mandatory API key is required. Hidden/shown preferences, optional notes, user-added papers, CCRF responses, and PDF previews stay in your browser unless you export them. A local profile label can separate browser-local collections on a shared computer. To let a colleague open the same Browse Papers curation, use Share Current Browse View; the link recreates that Browse setup without including local PDFs, CCRF responses, or notes. Analytics and PubMed surveillance may refresh from PubMed.

Start Here: Follow the guided walkthrough below to learn the main workflow: find and organise papers, add recent PubMed records, compare your collection with the wider literature, and prepare standardised CCRF research records.

A Simple, Browser-Local Workspace for Lipoedema Research

LipoScope brings together a starting library of 200 lipoedema papers, current PubMed searching, field-level analytics and the official CCRF Version 1 research workspace. Use it to find relevant papers, understand what has been studied, organise a focused reading set and prepare standardised research records.

Your hidden papers, added papers, notes, local PDF figure previews and CCRF records remain in this browser unless you choose to share or export them. LipoScope supports research planning and data organisation; it does not diagnose a patient or replace an institutionally governed data-capture system.

Find relevant papers Search the starting library by topic, study type, year, title, author, journal or findings, and add recent PubMed records through Live Search.
Keep a focused literature set Hide papers that are not relevant, restore them later, add notes and keep optional PDF figure previews on the same device.
See the wider research field Compare live PubMed publication trends with the papers currently visible in your Browse workspace.
Prepare standardised research records Use the official CCRF Version 1 classifications, review required-field gaps and export coded or readable datasets.
Work locally Most workspace changes remain in your browser unless you deliberately share a Browse link or download an export.
